title: Sliding Ladder Rate (10-meter ladder)
statement: A 10-meter ladder rests against a vertical wall. If the bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a rate of 1.2 m/s, how fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall when the bottom is 6 meters from the wall?
explanation: When $x = 6\text{ m}$, $y = \sqrt{100 - 36} = 8\text{ m}$. Differentiating $x^2 + y^2 = 100$ gives $x \frac{dx}{dt} + y \frac{dy}{dt} = 0$. Substituting $x = 6, y = 8, \frac{dx}{dt} = 1.2\text{ m/s}$: $6(1.2) + 8\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \implies 7.2 + 8\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \implies \frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{7.2}{8} = -0.9\text{ m/s}$. The top of the ladder is sliding down at $0.9\text{ m/s}$.

Formulate an equation relating the geometric variables.
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t using the chain rule, then substitute the given values.

title: Conical Tank Draining (Vertex Down)
statement: Water is leaking from a conical tank (vertex down) at a rate of 3 ft³/min. The tank has a height of 12 ft and a base radius of 6 ft. How fast is the water level falling when the water depth is 4 ft?
explanation: By similar triangles, $r/h = 6/12 = 1/2 \implies r = h/2$. Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi (h/2)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{12}h^3$. Differentiating: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{4}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = -3\text{ ft}^3/\text{min}$ and $h = 4\text{ ft}$: $-3 = \frac{\pi}{4}(16)\frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{3}{4\pi}\text{ ft/min} \approx -0.239\text{ ft/min}$.

title: Conical Tank Filling Rate
statement: Water is poured into a conical container at a rate of 10 cm³/sec. The cone points directly down and has a height of 30 cm and a base radius of 10 cm. How fast is the water level rising when the water is 9 cm deep?
explanation: Similar triangles: $r/h = 10/30 = 1/3 \implies r = h/3$. Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi (h/3)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{27}h^3$. Differentiating: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{9}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 10\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$ and $h = 9\text{ cm}$: $10 = \frac{\pi}{9}(81)\frac{dh}{dt} = 9\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{10}{9\pi}\text{ cm/s} \approx 0.354\text{ cm/s}$.

title: Streetlight Shadow Tip & Length Speed
statement: A man 6 feet tall walks away from a streetlight pole 15 feet high at a speed of 5 ft/s. How fast is the tip of his shadow moving, and how fast is the length of his shadow increasing?
explanation: Let $x$ be distance from pole and $s$ the shadow length. Similar triangles: $\frac{s}{6} = \frac{x + s}{15} \implies 15s = 6x + 6s \implies 9s = 6x \implies s = \frac{2}{3}x$. Differentiating: $\frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{2}{3}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{2}{3}(5) = \frac{10}{3}\text{ ft/s} \approx 3.33\text{ ft/s}$ (rate shadow length increases). Position of shadow tip from pole is $y = x + s = \frac{5}{3}x$. Rate tip moves: $\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{5}{3}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{5}{3}(5) = \frac{25}{3}\text{ ft/s} \approx 8.33\text{ ft/s}$.

title: Intersecting Cars Distance Rate
latexExpression: z^2 = x^2 + y^2 \implies z\frac{dz}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt}
statement: Car A is traveling west at 60 mi/h and Car B is traveling north at 80 mi/h toward the same intersection. At a given instant, Car A is 3 miles and Car B is 4 miles away from the intersection. At what rate is the distance between the two cars changing?
explanation: Let $x = 3\text{ mi}$ and $y = 4\text{ mi}$. Since both cars are moving toward the intersection, $\frac{dx}{dt} = -60\text{ mi/h}$ and $\frac{dy}{dt} = -80\text{ mi/h}$. Distance between cars $z = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\text{ miles}$. Differentiating $z^2 = x^2 + y^2$: $z \frac{dz}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} \implies 5\frac{dz}{dt} = 3(-60) + 4(-80) = -180 - 320 = -500 \implies \frac{dz}{dt} = -100\text{ mi/h}$. The distance is decreasing at $100\text{ mi/h}$.

title: Expanding Circular Oil Slick Area Rate
statement: An oil spill spreads in a circular pattern whose radius increases at a constant rate of 2 ft/min. How fast is the area of the oil slick increasing when the radius reaches 20 ft?
explanation: Area $A = \pi r^2$. Differentiating with respect to $t$: $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \frac{dr}{dt}$. Given $r = 20\text{ ft}$ and $\frac{dr}{dt} = 2\text{ ft/min}$: $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi(20)(2) = 80\pi\text{ ft}^2/\text{min} \approx 251.33\text{ ft}^2/\text{min}$.

title: Spherical Balloon Radius Growth Rate
statement: Air is pumped into a spherical balloon at a rate of 500 cm³/min. How fast is the radius of the balloon increasing when the radius is 10 cm?
explanation: Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \implies \frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \frac{dr}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 500\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$ and $r = 10\text{ cm}$: $500 = 4\pi (10)^2 \frac{dr}{dt} = 400\pi \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{500}{400\pi} = \frac{5}{4\pi}\text{ cm/min} \approx 0.398\text{ cm/min}$.

title: Spherical Balloon Surface Area Deflation Rate
statement: A spherical balloon is deflating at a rate of 30 cm³/sec. How fast is its surface area decreasing when the radius is 5 cm?
explanation: Volume: $\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dV/dt}{4\pi r^2}$. Surface area $S = 4\pi r^2 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} = 8\pi r \frac{dr}{dt} = 8\pi r \left(\frac{dV/dt}{4\pi r^2}\right) = \frac{2}{r}\frac{dV}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = -30\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$ and $r = 5\text{ cm}$: $\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{2}{5}(-30) = -12\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$. The surface area is decreasing at $12\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$.

title: Rotating Searchlight Beam Along Straight Shoreline
statement: A lighthouse is located 4 km off a straight shoreline. Its searchlight rotates at 3 rev/min (6π rad/min). How fast is the light beam moving along the shoreline at a point 3 km down the shore from the closest point?
explanation: Shoreline coordinate: $x = 4\tan\theta$. When $x = 3\text{ km}$, the distance from lighthouse is $D = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5\text{ km}$, so $\sec\theta = 5/4$ and $\sec^2\theta = 25/16$. Angular velocity $\frac{d\theta}{dt} = 6\pi\text{ rad/min}$. Rate of beam movement: $\frac{dx}{dt} = 4\sec^2\theta \frac{d\theta}{dt} = 4 \left(\frac{25}{16}\right)(6\pi) = \frac{75\pi}{2}\text{ km/min} \approx 117.81\text{ km/min}$.

title: Rocket Launch Radar Distance Tracking
latexExpression: D^2 = x^2 + y^2 = 25 + y^2 \implies D\frac{dD}{dt} = y\frac{dy}{dt}
statement: A rocket is launched vertically and is tracked from a radar station located on the ground 5 miles away from the launch pad. When the rocket is 12 miles high and rising at a speed of 4 mi/s, how fast is the distance between the radar station and the rocket increasing?
explanation: Distance from station $D = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = 13\text{ miles}$. Differentiating $D^2 = 25 + y^2$: $2D\frac{dD}{dt} = 2y\frac{dy}{dt} \implies D\frac{dD}{dt} = y\frac{dy}{dt}$. With $y = 12\text{ mi}$, $\frac{dy}{dt} = 4\text{ mi/s}$, and $D = 13\text{ mi}$: $13\frac{dD}{dt} = 12(4) = 48 \implies \frac{dD}{dt} = \frac{48}{13}\text{ mi/s} \approx 3.69\text{ mi/s}$.

title: Camera Angle of Elevation Rate for Model Rocket
statement: A camera is positioned 30 meters from the base of a launching platform. A model rocket is shot straight up at 10 m/s. How fast is the camera's angle of elevation changing when the rocket is 40 meters up?
explanation: At $y = 40\text{ m}$, distance to camera is $\sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = 50\text{ m}$. Thus $\cos\theta = 30/50 = 3/5 \implies \sec\theta = 5/3 \implies \sec^2\theta = 25/9$. Differentiating $\tan\theta = y/30$: $\sec^2\theta \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{1}{30}\frac{dy}{dt} \implies \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{1}{30\sec^2\theta}\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{9}{30(25)}(10) = \frac{90}{750} = \frac{3}{25} = 0.12\text{ rad/s}$.

title: Sand Pile Formation (Base Diameter = 3h)
statement: Dry sand pours from a conveyor belt at 10 m³/min, forming a conical pile whose base diameter is always equal to three times its height. How fast is the height of the pile increasing when the height is 4 meters?
explanation: Diameter $2r = 3h \implies r = \frac{3}{2}h$. Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{3}{2}h\right)^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{9}{4}h^2\right) h = \frac{3\pi}{4}h^3$. Differentiating: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{9\pi}{4}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 10\text{ m}^3/\text{min}$ and $h = 4\text{ m}$: $10 = \frac{9\pi}{4}(16)\frac{dh}{dt} = 36\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{10}{36\pi} = \frac{5}{18\pi}\text{ m/min} \approx 0.0884\text{ m/min}$.

title: Engine Crank and Piston Linear Velocity
statement: In an engine, a connecting rod is 12 inches long, attached to a crank of radius 4 inches rotating at 200 rad/min. Find the linear velocity of the piston when the crank angle is 90°.
explanation: Piston displacement $x = 4\cos\theta + \sqrt{144 - 16\sin^2\theta}$. Differentiating with respect to time: $\frac{dx}{dt} = \left[-4\sin\theta - \frac{32\sin\theta\cos\theta}{2\sqrt{144 - 16\sin^2\theta}}\right] \frac{d\theta}{dt}$. At $\theta = 90^\circ$: $\sin 90^\circ = 1$ and $\cos 90^\circ = 0$. The second term vanishes because $\cos 90^\circ = 0$. Thus $\frac{dx}{dt} = [-4(1) - 0](200) = -800\text{ in/min} \approx -66.67\text{ ft/min}$.

title: Triangular Cross-Section Water Trough
statement: A water trough is 10 meters long, and its cross-section is an isosceles triangle with a top width of 4 meters and a height of 3 meters. Water is being pumped in at 2 m³/min. How fast is the water level rising when the depth is 1.5 meters?
explanation: By similar triangles across the vertical cross-section: $\frac{w}{h} = \frac{4}{3} \implies w = \frac{4}{3}h$. Cross-sectional area of water $= \frac{1}{2}wh = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{4}{3}h\right)h = \frac{2}{3}h^2$. Total water volume $V = \text{Area} \times \text{Length} = \left(\frac{2}{3}h^2\right)(10) = \frac{20}{3}h^2$. Differentiating: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{40}{3}h \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 2\text{ m}^3/\text{min}$ and $h = 1.5\text{ m}$: $2 = \frac{40}{3}(1.5)\frac{dh}{dt} = 20\frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{2}{20} = 0.1\text{ m/min} = 10\text{ cm/min}$.

title: Particle Moving on Square Root Curve
statement: A particle moves along the curve $y = \sqrt{x}$. As it passes through the point (4, 2), its $y$-coordinate is increasing at a rate of 3 cm/s. How fast is its $x$-coordinate changing at that instant?
explanation: Differentiating $y = \sqrt{x}$ with respect to time $t$: $\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = 2\sqrt{x} \frac{dy}{dt}$. At $(4, 2)$, $x = 4$ and $\frac{dy}{dt} = 3\text{ cm/s}$: $\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\sqrt{4}(3) = 2(2)(3) = 12\text{ cm/s}$.

title: Rate of Change of Rectangle Diagonal
latexExpression: D^2 = x^2 + y^2 \implies D\frac{dD}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt}
statement: The length of a rectangle is increasing at a rate of 3 cm/s and its width is decreasing at a rate of 2 cm/s. When the length is 10 cm and width is 5 cm, how fast is the length of the diagonal changing?
explanation: Diagonal $D = \sqrt{10^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{100 + 25} = \sqrt{125} = 5\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}$. Differentiating $D^2 = x^2 + y^2$: $D\frac{dD}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt}$. Substituting $x = 10, y = 5, \frac{dx}{dt} = 3, \frac{dy}{dt} = -2$: $5\sqrt{5}\frac{dD}{dt} = 10(3) + 5(-2) = 30 - 10 = 20 \implies \frac{dD}{dt} = \frac{20}{5\sqrt{5}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5} \approx 1.789\text{ cm/s}$.

title: Inverted Square Pyramidal Tank Water Rate
statement: Water flows into an inverted square pyramidal tank at 5 m³/min. The base of the pyramid is a square of side 6 meters and the height is 12 meters. How fast is the water level rising when the depth is 4 meters?
explanation: Let $s$ be the side of the water square surface at depth $h$. By similar pyramids: $\frac{s}{h} = \frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2} \implies s = \frac{1}{2}h$. Volume of water $V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)^2 h = \frac{1}{12}h^3$. Differentiating: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{1}{4}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 5\text{ m}^3/\text{min}$ and $h = 4\text{ m}$: $5 = \frac{1}{4}(16)\frac{dh}{dt} = 4\frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25\text{ m/min}$.

title: Boat Approaching Dock on a Winch
statement: A boat is pulled toward a dock by a rope attached to the bow through a pulley located 5 feet above the bow. If the rope is hauled in at a rate of 2 ft/s, how fast is the boat approaching the dock when the rope is 13 feet long?
explanation: Right triangle with horizontal distance $x$, vertical height $5$, and hypotenuse $s = 13\text{ ft}$. When $s = 13$, $x = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12\text{ ft}$. Differentiating $x^2 + 25 = s^2$: $2x\frac{dx}{dt} = 2s\frac{ds}{dt} \implies x\frac{dx}{dt} = s\frac{ds}{dt}$. Given $\frac{ds}{dt} = -2\text{ ft/s}$: $12\frac{dx}{dt} = 13(-2) = -26 \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = -\frac{26}{12} = -\frac{13}{6}\text{ ft/s} \approx -2.17\text{ ft/s}$. The boat is approaching at $\frac{13}{6}\text{ ft/s}$.

title: Shadow of a Falling Ball from Light Source
statement: A ball is dropped from a height of 60 feet directly above a point 20 feet away from a light source on the ground. The height of the ball at time $t$ seconds is $h = 60 - 16t^2$. How fast is the length of the shadow on the ground changing when $t = 1$ second?
explanation: By similar triangles, $\frac{s}{20 + s} = \frac{h}{60} \implies 60s = 20h + sh \implies s(60 - h) = 20h \implies s = \frac{20h}{60 - h}$. When $t = 1\text{ s}$, $h = 60 - 16(1) = 44\text{ ft}$, and $\frac{dh}{dt} = -32t = -32\text{ ft/s}$. Differentiating $s(h)$: $\frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{20(60 - h) - 20h(-1)}{(60 - h)^2} \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{1200}{(60 - h)^2} \frac{dh}{dt}$. Substituting $h = 44$ and $\frac{dh}{dt} = -32$: $\frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{1200}{(16)^2}(-32) = \frac{1200}{256}(-32) = -\frac{1200}{8} = -150\text{ ft/s}$. The shadow length is shrinking at $150\text{ ft/s}$.

Formulate an equation relating the geometric variables.
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t using the chain rule, then substitute the given values.

title: Concentric Circular Ripples Area Change
statement: A pebble dropped into a calm pond causes concentric circular ripples. The outer ripple radius increases at 1 ft/s. How fast is the total area enclosed between the first and second ripples ($r_2 - r_1 = 2\text{ ft}$) changing?
explanation: Given $r_2 = r_1 + 2$, with both radii expanding at the same speed $\frac{dr_2}{dt} = \frac{dr_1}{dt} = 1\text{ ft/s}$. Area of the ring $A = \pi r_2^2 - \pi r_1^2 = \pi(r_2^2 - r_1^2)$. Differentiating with respect to time: $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r_2 \frac{dr_2}{dt} - 2\pi r_1 \frac{dr_1}{dt} = 2\pi(r_2 - r_1)(1) = 2\pi(2)(1) = 4\pi\text{ ft}^2/\text{s} \approx 12.57\text{ ft}^2/\text{s}$. Remarkably, this rate of area change is completely constant regardless of time!

title: Cylinder Volume Rate with Changing Radius and Height
statement: The radius of a right circular cylinder is increasing at 2 cm/min while its height is decreasing at 3 cm/min. How fast is the volume changing when radius is 5 cm and height is 10 cm?
explanation: Differentiating $V = \pi r^2 h$ using the product rule: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \pi\left(2rh\frac{dr}{dt} + r^2\frac{dh}{dt}\right)$. Given $r = 5\text{ cm}$, $h = 10\text{ cm}$, $\frac{dr}{dt} = 2\text{ cm/min}$, $\frac{dh}{dt} = -3\text{ cm/min}$: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \pi [2(5)(10)(2) + 5^2(-3)] = \pi [200 - 75] = 125\pi\text{ cm}^3/\text{min} \approx 392.7\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$. The volume is increasing at $125\pi\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$.

title: Two Ships Sailing Apart After 2 Hours
latexExpression: z^2 = x^2 + y^2 \implies z\frac{dz}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt}
statement: Ship A sails east from a port at 20 knots and Ship B sails south from the same port at 15 knots, starting at the same time. How fast is the distance between them increasing after 2 hours?
explanation: After $t = 2\text{ hours}$: $x = 20(2) = 40\text{ nm}$, $y = 15(2) = 30\text{ nm}$. Distance $z = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50\text{ nautical miles}$. Differentiating $z^2 = x^2 + y^2$: $z\frac{dz}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} \implies 50\frac{dz}{dt} = 40(20) + 30(15) = 800 + 450 = 1250 \implies \frac{dz}{dt} = \frac{1250}{50} = 25\text{ knots}$. (Since triangles remain similar, speed of separation is constant $\sqrt{20^2 + 15^2} = 25\text{ knots}$).

title: Ladder Slumping Midpoint Distance from Corner
statement: A beam of length 13 meters slides down between a vertical wall and a horizontal floor. If the top slides down at 0.5 m/s, how fast is the midpoint of the beam moving away from the corner when the base is 5 meters from the wall?
explanation: The midpoint coordinates are $(x/2, y/2)$. The distance from the corner $(0, 0)$ to the midpoint is $D = \sqrt{(x/2)^2 + (y/2)^2} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \frac{1}{2}(13) = 6.5\text{ meters}$. Because $x^2 + y^2 = L^2$ is constant, the distance from the origin to the midpoint of the sliding beam is ALWAYS constant ($L/2 = 6.5\text{ m}$). Therefore, $\frac{dD}{dt} = 0\text{ m/s}$. The midpoint travels along a circle of radius 6.5 m centered at the corner, so its distance from the corner does not change at all!

title: Parabolic Bowl Liquid Level Draining Rate
statement: Liquid drains from a parabolic bowl $y = x^2$ at 2 cm³/sec. How fast is the liquid level dropping when the depth is 4 cm?
explanation: The bowl is formed by rotating $y = x^2$ about the $y$-axis. The circular cross-sectional slice at depth $y$ has area $A(y) = \pi x^2 = \pi y$. Volume of liquid up to depth $y$ is $V = \int_0^y \pi u\,du = \frac{\pi}{2}y^2$. Differentiating with respect to $t$: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \pi y \frac{dy}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = -2\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$ and $y = 4\text{ cm}$: $-2 = \pi (4) \frac{dy}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{2}{4\pi} = -\frac{1}{2\pi}\text{ cm/s} \approx -0.159\text{ cm/s}$. The level drops at $\frac{1}{2\pi}\text{ cm/s}$.

title: Airplane Flying Overhead Radar Distance Rate
statement: An airplane flies horizontally at an altitude of 6 miles and a speed of 500 mi/h directly over a radar station. How fast is the distance between the airplane and the radar station increasing 1 minute after it passes overhead?
explanation: Time elapsed: $1\text{ minute} = 1/60\text{ hr}$. Horizontal distance traveled: $x = 500 \times (1/60) = 25/3\text{ miles} \approx 8.33\text{ mi}$. Altitude $y = 6\text{ miles}$. Distance to radar $D = \sqrt{6^2 + (25/3)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 625/9} = \sqrt{949/9} = \frac{\sqrt{949}}{3} \approx 10.27\text{ miles}$. Differentiating $D^2 = 36 + x^2$: $D\frac{dD}{dt} = x\frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dD}{dt} = \frac{x}{D}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{25/3}{\sqrt{949}/3}(500) = \frac{12500}{\sqrt{949}} \approx 405.77\text{ mi/h}$.
hints: Draw a diagram and assign variable names to all quantities changing with time.
Formulate an equation relating the geometric variables.
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t using the chain rule, then substitute the given values.
